ai_context.summary: Fix crow usage data (synthetic pricing, account-named titles, split rtk databases), give every session a Haiku title, surface per-tool savings, and lay the usage view out responsively with tabs; mirror it in the archeotech bar panels.
ai_context.use when: changing crow-usage/crow-runs JSON, the crow watch TUI, or the archeotech crow-agents/crow-usage modules.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Session cost ignores `<synthetic>` and other unpriced pseudo-models instead of voiding the session; a session is unpriced only when a real model has no price, and day totals flag unpriced sessions rather than silently counting $0.

- AC2: Every session in `crow-usage --json` and every session agent in `crow-runs json` has a `title`: the dispatch label for runs, otherwise a 3-6 word Haiku title generated from the first user prompts, cached by session id in local/state and refreshed when the session has grown substantially; titles never block a poll (generation is async and bounded per poll).
- AC3: rtk savings are read from every rtk history database (real HOME and each cdx profile) and summed, so the TUI and the bar show the same numbers.
- AC4: Usage 'active' agrees with the agents board for sessions the board knows about.
- AC5: The usage payload splits tokens into input, output, cache write and cache read per session and per day, and exposes week totals; the TUI and panel show a totals row and the split.

- AC6: Savings and retros get a named section with plain labels (e.g. 'rtk: 58k tokens trimmed from command output today', 'retros: 2 sessions reviewed today, 0 suggestions awaiting your OK'), moved out of the key-help footer.
Needs: - The usage numbers must be right before they are worth designing around: today's cost and the 7-day chart currently undercount, and every session is titled with the account name.
- Each session needs a short human title so 'top sessions today' says what the tokens were spent on instead of listing 'cr-0w' eight times.
- Information that matters (tool savings, retros, proposals) must be visible and labelled in plain words, not tucked next to the key help.
- The owner wants to judge whether each token-saving tool (rtk, prompt cache, model routing, scripts) pays off, with numbers that can be tracked over time.
- The usage view must use the space of a tall or vertical terminal without hiding things in sub-menus, and still degrade cleanly on small terminals.
- Redundant UI should go: a gauge that already shows 1 of 2 slots doesn't need '1/2' next to it.

ai_context.summary: Fix crow-usage pricing of synthetic messages, Haiku session titles cached by id, rtk read across all history databases, active-state agreement, token split and week totals.
ai_context.use when: changing bin/crow-usage or the title field in crow-runs json.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: no session with a priced real model has cost null; synthetic messages are skipped.
- AC2: every session has a non-account title; runs use their dispatch label; generation is cached, async and bounded.
- AC3: rtk totals equal the sum over all history databases.
- AC4: usage active state matches crow-runs for known sessions.
- AC5: per-session and per-day token split plus week totals in the JSON payload.
Problem: - Costs undercount because one `<synthetic>` message voids a whole session's price.
- Sessions are all titled with the account name, so nothing tells them apart.
- rtk numbers depend on which HOME reads them, and 'active' means different things in the two views.
